removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file homotopy.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 576-579 (book Lemma 8.1.7): for every point x of the circle and every path p from the base point to x, decoding the encoding of p returns p. The statement is an identity between composites over an arbitrary point, and the proof (source lines 580-587) first uses path induction to reduce it to the reflexivity path at the base point, where the two composites have to be unfolded by definition: encoding reflexivity is transport of the canonical integer along reflexivity, hence zero, and decoding zero is the zeroth power of the generating loop, hence reflexivity. Which definitions have to be unfolded, and why the general case needs no further argument, is the content and the statement shows none of it.

removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 665-667: the total space of the circle code is contractible. The statement is a single contractibility claim, and the proof (source lines 668-699) is a construction: it first applies the flattening lemma with an explicit choice of span, family and equivalence to identify the total space with a higher inductive type generated by a point for each integer and a path between consecutive points, then proves that type contractible by choosing the point at zero as centre and building, by induction on the integers, a path from the centre to every generator, and finally verifies the path constructor by showing that the constructed path concatenated with the generator equals the next constructed path, again by induction. The author calls that last verification easy, which this card records verbatim; the flattening application and the two inductions are the substance and none of them is visible in the statement.

removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 8.2.1 at source lines 801-802: if A is n-connected then its suspension is (n+1)-connected, proved across source lines 805-870. The proof first has to translate the goal into contractibility of trunc(n+1)(1 sqcup^A 1) (source line 809) and then invoke that truncation of a pushout cocone is a pushout among truncated types to move to the diagram whose vertices are all the point (source lines 811-821). The load-bearing part is the verification that the point is a pushout of that diagram: the cocone type has to be rewritten as Sm{x:E}{y:E}(x =_E y) in two steps, first using that trunc(n+1)A is n-connected while the path type of an (n+1)-truncated E is n-truncated (source lines 840-845), and then using that E is equivalent to that total space (source lines 851-857). Only after that chain can uniqueness of pushouts be applied (source lines 867-869). The statement records none of this: the reduction to a pushout and the two truncation-level bookkeeping steps are the content.

removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 1080-1093 (book Theorem 8.4.6): a pointed map f : X \to Y with fiber F gives a long exact sequence of homotopy groups, which are groups except in the last three terms and abelian except in the last six. The statement records only the sequence and the algebraic structure, while the proof (source lines 1100-1129) has to establish exactness at every term: it reduces the theorem to exactness of the 0-truncation of a fiber sequence, proves the inclusion im \subseteq ker from functoriality together with f \circ g = 0, and then has to show ker \subseteq im for an element given only as a truncated equality, which forces two successive truncation inductions: one to lift the element of the 0-truncation to an element w of W, and one that uses the path-truncation equivalence to turn \tproj0{f(w)} = \tproj0{z_0} into a genuine path p : f(w) = z_0, after which (w,p) is the required preimage. The identification of the later maps with the negative of the induced maps on homotopy groups, and the resulting group and abelian-group structure, are then read off with thm:fiber-of-the-fiber and the Eckmann-Hilton argument; nothing of this reduction is visible in the statement.

removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 8.6.1 at source lines 1569-1572: for an n-connected f and a family P of k-types with k >= n, the precomposition map (blank o f) is (k-n-2)-truncated, proved at source lines 1574-1590. The proof inducts on k - n with the fixed-level induction principle as base case (source line 1576) and then has to make the level drop by exactly one. That requires computing the fibre of (blank o f) at a section l as Sm{g : Prd{b:B}P(b)} Prd{a:A} g(f(a)) = l(a) (line 1580), computing the identity type of two such pairs as Sm{r : g ~ h} (r o f = p . q^-1) (lines 1582-1584), and then recognising that last type as the fibre of the same precomposition map for the family Q(b) := (g(b) = h(b)) (lines 1585-1587). The variable level is what makes this non-routine: the statement shifts the truncation index at each induction step, and the fibre and identity-type computations have to be set up so that their own level drops accordingly.
